lead.t: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO): Consider for refractory severe ARDS in specialised centres.

snip.t: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (ECMO): Consider for refractory severe ARDS in specialised centres.

Surfactant use does not appear to affect mortality rates, it may reduce the severity of disease, progression to extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) utilization,  and decrease the length of hospital stay.

qs.q: When is extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) typically utilized in the management of an infant with meconium aspiration syndrome?
o: When all other conventional therapeutic options have been exhausted
Immediately following confirmation of meconium-stained amniotic fluid
When surfactant administration fails to improve oxygenation within one hour
As an immediate first-line intervention for severe parenchymal lung disease
qs.e: ECMO is used if all other therapeutic options have been exhausted, keeping in mind that it is associated with a high incidence of poor neurologic outcomes. It is never used as an initial first-line therapy.
